### [Direct Preference Optimization: Your Language Model is Secretly a Reward Model](<https://arxiv.org/abs/2305.18290>)

Direct Preference Optimization converts a regularized preference-learning objective into a direct loss on preferred and rejected responses, avoiding a separately trained reward model and online policy rollouts. It remains a useful foundational baseline for aligning model behavior from offline preference pairs with a comparatively simple training pipeline.

**Published:** 2023-05-29 · **First seen:** 2026-09-30T04:09:33Z · **Novelty:** baseline · **Tags:** Preference Optimization, Alignment, DPO

**Positioning:** established-method

[Paper](<https://arxiv.org/abs/2305.18290>) · [Code](<https://github.com/eric-mitchell/direct-preference-optimization>)

**Evidence:** research-paper; full-text. The paper derives the objective and evaluates sentiment control, summarization, and single-turn dialogue against reinforcement-learning and supervised baselines; an author reference implementation is available.

**Limitations:** Its preference-model assumptions and dependence on offline data matter; the original experiments do not establish universal superiority to online RL or robustness under distribution shift.
